jobs.descriptionHtml:
Scribd, Inc. is on a mission to advance human understanding. Our four products — Scribd®, Slideshare®, Everand™, and Fable — help billions of people across the globe move beyond access and into insight, application, and expertise.

Culture at Scribd, Inc.

We support a culture where our employees can be real and be bold; where we debate and commit as we embrace plot twists; and where every employee is empowered to take action as we prioritize the customer.

We believe the best work happens when individual flexibility is balanced with meaningful community connection. Scribd Flex empowers employees to choose the workstyle and location that support their best performance, while committing to intentional in-person moments that strengthen collaboration and culture. Occasional in-person attendance is required for all Scribd, Inc. employees, regardless of location.

So what are we looking for in new team members? At Scribd, Inc., we hire for “GRIT.” Traditionally defined as the intersection of passion and perseverance toward long-term goals, GRIT reflects the mindset we expect from every employee. For us, it also serves as a practical framework for how we work: setting and achieving Goals, delivering Results within your role, contributing Innovative ideas and solutions, and strengthening the broader Team through collaboration and attitude.

This posting reflects an approved, open position within the organization.

About the team and role

Welcome to our small but mighty TPM (Technical Program Management) team! We are the driving force that shapes how our company plans, prioritizes, and executes. As a Senior TPM, you will own program strategy and execution across our marketing organization, which owns two key pillars of work: Customer Operations and Brand Marketing.

Customer Operations is the pillar that reflects the voice of the customer back to the company, and the one that works to deliver an effortless customer support experience. You will partner with its leadership to drive the programs that connect that work to the rest of the company, from the voice of the customer program, to how that support experience is designed and delivered end to end, to the evolution of the operational model and team structure for Premium support.

Brand Marketing is the pillar that helps the company build and sustain brands people love and want to tell their friends about. You will act as the connector between brand strategy and product strategy and execution, working across stakeholders to design the processes, workflows, and tools that make sure the personality and identity of our brands are felt in the product itself and in our messaging and communications, which include larger brand campaigns as well as always-on communications.

You will drive the roadmap across both, connect them to the teams and leaders that depend on them, and bring a builder's instinct to the work, using AI and creative workflows to design better ways of running these programs.

About you

You are a thoughtful opinionator: you hold strong, well-reasoned views and are capable of voicing them respectfully to anyone, at any level. You are a proactive communicator who identifies possible problems before they surface.

You are a relationship builder and organizational navigator at heart, adept at building bridges across teams and functions. You are comfortable working with customer experience, marketing, and creative teams as well as product and engineering, able to follow the substance and hold your own with the subject matter experts you partner with.

You care about customers and about the power of building strong brands. You understand what a great customer experience is worth to a company, and you are intellectually curious about how brand personality and identity show up in consumer-facing products. You have been part of efforts that connected brand strategy to how a product is built and experienced.

You are already working with AI, and you have a point of view on where the TPM craft is headed in an increasingly agentic world. You have changed how you operate because of it.

You are a continuous learner with a growth mindset and an appetite for unfamiliar problems. Lastly, you are a voracious reader with a passion for books and the written and spoken word in all its forms!

What you will do

  • Act like an owner: Be an owner of program strategy and execution across our Customer Operations and Brand Marketing pillars, and serve as the connective tissue between those pillars and the partners they depend on.

  • Build relationships: Our TPM team thrives on collaboration. You will work closely with stakeholders at every level, from customer experience and marketing teams to engineers and executives, and your ability to build trust and align diverse perspectives will be central to what you can accomplish.

  • Drive strategy: You will dive deep into the how and the why of your programs, developing plans that connect day-to-day execution to where these pillars need to go. Your judgment will shape how decisions get made.

  • Decide what's worth doing: Partner with Customer Operations leadership to prioritize projects by customer impact, weigh them against team capacity, and defer or decline the rest. The customer's experience stays at the center of every tradeoff.

  • Connect marketing and product: Act as a connector between our marketing organization and our product-centric teams, working across stakeholders to design the processes, workflows, and tools that make sure brand is part of our key releases, in the product experience itself and in the messaging and communications around it.

  • Be a leader: Act as a leader within the TPM team. Identify opportunities to collaborate, share what works, and coach your teammates.

  • Lead beyond your pillars: Our TPM team also owns cross-company processes like yearly planning. You will contribute to these shared efforts and take a leadership role in shaping them.

  • Own the complexity: Drive multiple complex cross-functional programs simultaneously, and create scalable frameworks across pillars and functions to track work and communicate progress.

  • Enable your drivers: Many of the people driving and contributing to Customer Operations initiatives are also handling day to day frontline work and escalations. You will plan around their real capacity and give them structure and support, rather than assigning tasks and chasing updates.

  • Manage timelines: Lead the delivery timeline for your programs. Proactively identify risks and create mitigation strategies through workflows, communication, or resource allocation.

  • Measure success: Proactively propose success metrics for yourself and your programs, and identify when those metrics are at risk.

  • Build to move faster: Use AI and lightweight tooling to reduce the coordination tax on your teams. When you spot a manual, repetitive process, build something better.

  • Improve how we work: Identify and drive process improvements at the team and cross-team level, so the whole organization delivers at a larger scale.

We're looking for

  • 5+ years of experience in a program management, operations, or equivalent role at a technology company.

  • A track record of operating independently, leading through ambiguity, and navigating complex organizational dynamics.

  • A structured approach to your work, paired with the judgment to know when to add process and when to remove it to reduce overhead and drive velocity.

  • Experience partnering closely with customer operations, marketing, or brand teams, and connecting their work to product and engineering teams.

  • An understanding of what great customer support is worth to a brand, and enough knowledge of brand to hold your own with marketers. You have worked with customer support teams, or know their workflows well enough to be a useful partner to them.

  • A customer-first lens in how you make decisions, with the judgment to weigh customer impact against efficiency.

  • Experience rolling out operational changes, such as process and tooling to a frontline team.

  • Strong familiarity with the software development process, working with product and engineering teams from roadmapping through delivery.

  • Experience working directly with product managers, engineers, marketers, and other subject matter experts.

  • Hands-on experience using AI in your work, and a clear point of view on how it changes the program management craft. You have already adjusted how you operate because of it.

  • Experience using data to identify problems and communicate solutions.

  • The ability to work and partner successfully across multiple functions in an organization.

  • Excellent communication and interpersonal skills.

  • Exceptional attention to detail and the ability to understand and articulate the big picture.

  • Distinctive problem-solving and analytical skills.

Bonus Points

  • You have held a program management role at a company where customer support sits at the heart of the brand.

  • You have seen up close how great customer support works, even if you have not worked in it directly.

  • You have run or helped run brand campaigns.

  • You have worked in a brand or marketing role earlier in your career.

  • You have designed AI workflows that enable customer operations or brand marketing teams to do their best work, whether that meant changing how a team handles its day-to-day or building something foundational they now can't imagine working without.

----------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Our pay ranges are based on the local cost of labor benchmarks for each specific role, level, and geographic location. San Francisco is our highest geographic market in the United States.

 

In the state of California, the reasonably expected salary range is between $124,000 [minimum salary in our lowest geographic market within California] to $172,000[maximum salary in our highest geographic market within California].

 

In the United States, outside of California, the reasonably expected salary range is between $102,000 [minimum salary in our lowest US geographic market outside of California] to $164,000 [maximum salary in our highest US geographic market outside of California].

 

In Canada, the reasonably expected salary range is between $131,000 CAD[minimum salary in our lowest geographic market] to $152,000 CAD[maximum salary in our highest geographic market].

 

We carefully consider a wide range of factors when determining compensation, including but not limited to experience; job-related skill sets; relevant education or training; and other business and organizational needs. The salary range listed is for the level at which this job has been scoped. In the event that you are considered for a different level, a higher or lower pay range would apply. This position is also eligible for a competitive equity ownership, and a comprehensive and generous benefits package.

  • Comprehensive health, dental, and vision coverage

  • Generous paid time off, including vacation, sick time, holidays, winter break, volunteer time, and sabbaticals

  • Paid parental leave and family support benefits

  • Retirement matching and employee equity

  • Strong understanding of conversion optimization, audience targeting, and creative testing methodologies

  • Experience with attribution models and incrementality testing; able to pressure-test data and validate what actually drove performance before scaling

  • In-depth understanding of automated bid strategies with experience optimizing toward CPA or ROAS goals

  • Comfortable using AI tools in your day-to-day workflow (Ex: for creative concepting, performance analysis, or experimentation) and genuinely curious about how emerging tools change what's possible

  • Excellent analytical skills with proficiency in data visualization tools

  • Track record of cross-functional collaboration and stakeholder management

  • Experience marketing subscription products or digital content services

  • Google Tag Manager experience

  • Familiarity with mobile app marketing and app store optimization

  • Familiarity and eagerness to work with AI tools

  • The Content Library is one of the more interesting storage problems you'll find anywhere.   • The core of the platform is written in Rust and built on the excellent Rust data ecosystem (Apache Arrow, Parquet, and DataFusion), with a Python "userland" that teams across the company contribute to directly. If you want a taste of the work, read about Content Crush on our tech blog: https://tech.scribd.com/blog/2026/content-crush.html

  • This role will join an existing team of Senior, Staff, and Principal engineers building the Content Library and Core Infrastructure of Scribd, Inc. for all our production datastores. Working alongside the Content Library's architect and lead engineer, you'll take ownership of the application codebase, drive feature development forward, and help shape where the platform goes as it becomes the foundation for all content at Scribd, Inc.

About you:

  • You're a systems engineer who loves owning software end-to-end: design, implementation, deployment, operations, and the inevitable "why is this slow?" investigations.

  • You're pragmatic about technology choices; you keep things simple, and you write things down. Design docs, runbooks, and thoughtful code reviews are how you scale yourself.

  • You enjoy being the engineer other teams come to, whether that's reviewing their contributions, unblocking an integration, or turning an ambiguous ask into well-scoped work.

  • You've made agentic AI tools part of your daily engineering practice, and you know they accelerate great engineers rather than replace engineering judgment. Humans stay in the loop on quality, security, and ownership.

What you will do:

  • Design, build, and operate the Content Library's core Rust services (transactional storage, transform coordination, and low-latency retrieval paths) at the scale of hundreds of billions of objects.

  • Own features end-to-end, from technical design through implementation, testing, deployment, and production operations (observability, on-call, and incident response for the systems you own).

  • Evolve the Python userland (the transform framework, tooling, and developer experience) and support engineers across the company who build on the platform through code reviews, guidance, and well-designed APIs.

  • Lead cross-functional projects with stakeholders in ML, search, product, and data teams: defining roadmaps, milestones, and technical designs that balance scalability, performance, cost, and delivery.

  • Drive performance and cost-efficiency across the stack: query execution (DataFusion), Parquet file layouts, S3 access patterns, caching strategies, and PostgreSQL/Aurora tuning.

  • Strengthen the platform's governance capabilities: data lineage, authorization and access controls, and deletion propagation across brands.

  • Raise the engineering bar on the team through mentorship, design reviews, and improvements to our developer environment, including making agentic AI workflows more effective within our codebase while preserving quality, security, and ownership.

Requirements:

  • 10+ years of professional software engineering experience building backend, distributed, or data-intensive systems.

  • Production experience writing Rust and strong proficiency in Python.

  • A deep understanding of storage and data fundamentals: object storage (S3), columnar formats (Apache Parquet/Arrow), and relational databases (PostgreSQL and/or MySQL).

  • A track record of designing and operating high-throughput, low-latency services, including the operational side: metrics, tracing, alerting, and debugging production systems.

  • Demonstrated technical leadership: leading projects across team boundaries, writing design docs that build alignment, and mentoring engineers.

  • Experience with AWS (e.g., S3, Lambda, ECS, Aurora) and infrastructure-as-code workflows (e.g., Terraform).

  • Clear communication with both technical and non-technical stakeholders, and comfort turning ambiguous requirements into shipped software.

Ideally, you have:

  • Direct experience with Apache DataFusion, arrow-rs, the parquet crate, or building query engines and database internals.

  • Contributions to open source, especially in the Rust data ecosystem (delta-rs, Arrow, DataFusion, etc.).

  • Experience with data governance at scale: lineage, access control, GDPR and deletion compliance.

  • A FinOps mindset: you've bent a cloud bill downward through architecture, not just instance right-sizing.

  • Experience building platforms that other engineers build on: SDKs, contribution models, and paved-road developer experience.

  • Recent, hands-on investment in agentic engineering practices, using tools like Claude Code as a core part of your development workflow while keeping human review at the center of quality and security.

  • A collaborator who communicates early and often with cross-functional partners to align on goals and tradeoffs.

  • A pragmatic problem-solver who balances technical rigor with business impact.

  • An engineer who cares deeply about users and turns that care into the features they build.

Required Qualifications

  • 5+ years of experience shipping iOS apps to the public, including consumer apps at scale.

  • Strong proficiency in Swift, with deep experience in SwiftUI and UIKit.

  • Comfort working in a mature codebase that still has Objective-C.

  • Experience building in-app purchase or subscription features with StoreKit, and knowledge of the App Store rules that apply to them.

  • Experience designing, building, and consuming APIs (REST, GraphQL a plus).

  • A track record of addressing technical debt and migrating code to newer technologies without slowing delivery.

  • Excellent communication skills and ability to lead technical initiatives in a collaborative environment.

  • Payments: StoreKit and StoreKit 2, App Store subscriptions

  • Testing: XCTest, XCUITest (or similar)

  • API Integration: RESTful APIs, JSON, GraphQL

  • Tooling: Xcode, Git, and iOS CI/CD

  • Experience with subscription systems, payments, or retention features such as paywalls, trials, cancellation and save flows, or win-back.

  • You are equally comfortable as the modeler and the analyst. You can build the pipeline, define the metric, and defend the number in a room full of executives.

  • You communicate early and plainly, and you write things down. Methodology and model documentation are part of the deliverable.

  • Own the canonical data models for payments, billing, and subscriptions in Databricks modeled once across Scribd, Everand, and Fable so a new market, or payment method doesn't require a rewrite, and built with the next engineer and the AI tools on top as explicit consumers.

  • Build AI tools on trusted foundations, grounded in certified metrics and tables, kept in sync as definitions change, and validated with evaluation sets that prove the answers are right.

  • Raise the technical bar, set modeling and metric conventions, influence source-system changes before they land, and mentor analysts and analytics engineers in these domains.

  • 8+ years of experience in analytics engineering, data engineering, business intelligence engineering or a related discipline

  • Deep, hands-on payments expertise: including direct experience with processor data from Stripe, Adyen, Braintree, PayPal, or similar.

  • Practical experience with identity and authentication data

  • Depth in governed, canonical data models and semantic layers, and a track record of defining a metric, defending it under scrutiny, and versioning it when its inputs changed.

  • Advanced SQL and production experience with Databricks, AWS, Looker, Airbyte, Fivetran, or comparable platforms, including orchestration, transformation frameworks, and automated testing.

  • Experience making data reliable for AI consumption

  • Proven ability to influence senior product and engineering leaders and translate complex payment economics into clear business trade-offs.

  • Advanced Python and experience building AI agents or LLM-based pipelines.

  • Define and improve secrets management, data protection, and encryption standards, ensuring security controls are effective and their coverage can be demonstrated.

Secure cloud workloads and delivery paths

  • Drive security architecture and guardrails for cloud workloads, including Kubernetes, secure base images, workload identity, runtime protection, and isolation of services processing untrusted content, with an emphasis on limiting the impact of compromise.

  • Partner with our Infrastructure teams to secure cloud deployment paths, workload identities, registries, and the infrastructure supporting CI/CD.

  • Build reusable security capabilities and paved paths, including Terraform modules and policy-as-code guardrails, that make secure configurations the default and prevent noncompliant infrastructure changes before deployment.

Strengthen cloud visibility and resilience

  • Define cloud telemetry requirements and improve detection coverage for cloud-native threats in partnership with Detection & Response.

  • Validate cloud security controls through threat hunting and attack-path analysis, contribute technical expertise during incidents, and partner with infrastructure teams on containment and recovery architecture, translating incident learnings into durable improvements.

Drive Cloud Security strategy and technical direction

  • Provide technical guidance and mentorship, contribute to tooling evaluations, and proactively communicate Cloud Security risks, progress, and direction to stakeholders.

Deep expertise in at least one of AWS or GCP, with sufficient fluency in the other to reason about security risks.

  • Experience shaping security architecture and leading initiatives across team boundaries, including influencing engineering teams to adopt security standards and controls without formal authority.

  • Deep hands-on identity and access management expertise, including least-privilege access, cross-account access patterns, short-lived workload credentials (e.g., IRSA, OIDC federation), and service-to-service identity and authorization (e.g., mTLS, SPIFFE/SPIRE, or service mesh identity models), with experience reducing standing access and long-lived credentials.

  • Experience securing cloud workloads, including Kubernetes, container security, runtime protection, and workload isolation.

  • Experience with cloud security posture management and workload protection, including CSPM/CNAPP platforms, evaluating security findings, identifying attack paths, and translating them into prioritized improvements.

  • Experience designing and implementing cloud security guardrails at scale, including account or project security baselines, policy-as-code (e.g., AWS SCPs or OPA), secure infrastructure provisioning, and landing zone automation.

  • Strong Infrastructure-as-Code and automation skills, including Terraform or equivalent tooling and proficiency in a programming language such as Python or Go.

  • Experience with cloud security visibility and response, including cloud-native security tooling (e.g., GuardDuty, Security Command Center, CloudTrail, or Cloud Audit Logs), detection capabilities, SIEM integration, and applying incident learnings to improve preventive and detective controls.

  • Partner closely with the teams that own support tooling, automation/AI, and product to turn customer feedback into better tools and product decisions, and keep bug triage and escalation handoffs running smoothly

  • Drive operational change and continuous improvement alongside the Customer Operations leadership team, introducing new tools, processes, and ways of working that make support better for customers and for the team

About the Team

The Payments & Billing team at Scribd powers our subscription revenue engine by delivering the systems that manage billing lifecycles, global payment processing, and financial reliability across Scribd, Everand, Slideshare, and Fable. Our focus areas include payment processing at scale, invoicing, reconciliation, fraud prevention, compliance, and support for international currencies and payment methods. We partner closely with Product, Finance, Risk, and Platform Engineering to ensure that millions of readers worldwide can reliably access our services every day.

We're an agentic engineering team. AI agents (Claude Code, shared agent skills, and integrations with tools like Datadog, Sentry, and Stripe) are part of how we design, build, test, triage, and operate every day. Because our systems move money and sit in PCI scope, we hold AI-generated work to the same human-review, correctness, and security bar as anything else we ship.

What You'll Do

  • Lead the technical architecture and implementation of Scribd's payments and billing systems, the backbone of our subscription business.

  • Design, build, and operate backend services that power subscription payments at global scale.

  • Own billing lifecycle, global payments, invoicing, reconciliation, and financial reliability, integrating with multiple providers (Stripe, Adyen, Braintree) and supporting international currencies and local methods.

  • Ensure compliance and security of financial systems through PCI DSS, tokenization, encryption, and secure data handling.

  • Lead agentic engineering on the team: use AI agents across design, implementation, testing, debugging, and operations, and help the team adopt workflows that make us measurably faster without lowering the bar on correctness or security.

  • Build shared AI leverage for payments, such as agent skills for alert triage, incident investigation, and anomaly detection, and runbooks, documentation, and context that agents can use reliably. Contribute these to Scribd's shared skills marketplace rather than building one-off tools.

  • Define guardrails for AI-assisted changes in PCI scope: human review of every change, keeping cardholder and sensitive data out of prompts, logs, and unapproved tools, and clear testing and verification standards for AI-generated code that touches money movement.

  • Foster a culture of technical excellence while driving scalable, resilient, and observable financial systems that enable teams to move fast, simplify complexity, and deliver revenue with confidence.

  • Modernize legacy systems and eliminate technical debt to improve velocity and scalability, using AI agents to accelerate migrations, refactors, and test coverage where they make sense.

  • Partner with Product, Finance, Risk, Platform, and Analytics to deliver secure, reliable financial flows, leveraging data, metrics, and telemetry to uncover trends, resolve anomalies, and guide the team with clarity and foresight.

  • Mentor engineers, shape cross-team technical strategy, and tackle some of the hardest scaling and security challenges in the company, including raising the bar on how the team designs, reviews, and verifies AI-assisted work.

We're Looking for Someone Who

Premium is the Scribd Inc. pillar behind two reading products: Everand, the audiobook and ebook subscription app, and Fable, the social app where readers track, discuss and discover books. You'll join Premium's new Discovery squad. It's a small, dedicated group of recommendations, search, applied research and ML engineers working full time on discovery for Everand and Fable. The squad works closely with Orion, Scribd's ML platform team. Orion runs the feature store, model registry, embedding-based retrieval and model serving behind discovery across Scribd, Slideshare and Everand.

We're looking for a Senior Machine Learning Engineer to own recommendations for Fable and grow into the technical lead for Premium recommendations.

Fable's recommender today is a collaborative-filtering model built in house. It has served readers well, but it has no real-time signals and no learned ranking, and it can't recommend to new or lapsed readers. Your first big project is to move Fable onto Orion, so Fable and Everand share a modern recommendation stack.

Key responsibilities

  • Lead the migration of Fable's recommendations onto Orion, covering data, features, training, serving and experiments, while keeping today's recommendations running.

  • Extend Orion's rankers, feature store and embedding-based retrieval to support Fable, in partnership with the Orion ML platform team.

  • Own the health of Fable's recommendation systems in production: quality, latency, cost and on-call.

  • Bring Fable's social signals (shelves, ratings, reviews, book clubs, reader similarity) into recommendations for both Fable and Everand.

  • Design and analyze A/B tests with product managers and analysts to decide what ships.

  • Act as technical lead for Premium recommendations. Shape the roadmap with product managers, and see work that depends on other teams' systems through to delivery.

  • Raise the bar on engineering practice in the squad through design reviews, code quality and operational readiness.

Tech you'll work with

You'll work across two stacks: Fable's on Google Cloud and Orion's on AWS.

  • Fable: Python (FastAPI, Django), PostgreSQL, BigQuery, Kubernetes, Google Cloud including Vertex AI

  • Orion and Everand: Python, Go and gRPC, Ruby on Rails, Databricks and Spark, Airflow, AWS SageMaker, Weaviate for embedding-based retrieval, feature store and model registry

  • Infrastructure: AWS (EKS, ECS, Lambda, SQS, ElastiCache), Datadog, Terraform

Requirements

Must have

  • 5+ years as a professional ML or software engineer, with a track record of shipping production ML systems.

  • Hands-on experience building and running recommender systems in production, such as collaborative filtering or matrix factorization, two-tower or embedding retrieval, and learned ranking.

  • Experience with large-scale data processing (Spark, Databricks, BigQuery or similar).

  • Experience on at least one major cloud (AWS or GCP), including deploying services on containers (Kubernetes, ECS or similar).

  • Experience designing and analyzing online experiments.

  • A record of leading projects that depend on other teams, and of working directly with product managers.

  • Bachelor's or Master's degree in Computer Science, or equivalent professional experience.

Nice to have

  • Google Cloud experience, especially Vertex AI and BigQuery.

  • Experience migrating or replacing a production ML system while keeping it running.

  • Social or graph-based recommendations, such as user similarity, follows or groups.

  • Search and semantic retrieval (Elasticsearch, Vertex AI Search, vector databases).

We support a culture where our employees can be real and be bold; where we debate and commit as we embrace plot twists; and where every employee is empowered to take action as we prioritize the customer.

We believe the best work happens when individual flexibility is balanced with meaningful community connection. Scribd Flex empowers employees to choose the workstyle and location that support their best performance, while committing to intentional in-person moments that strengthen collaboration and culture. Occasional in-person attendance is required for all Scribd, Inc. employees, regardless of location.

So what are we looking for in new team members? At Scribd, Inc., we hire for “GRIT.” Traditionally defined as the intersection of passion and perseverance toward long-term goals, GRIT reflects the mindset we expect from every employee. For us, it also serves as a practical framework for how we work: setting and achieving Goals, delivering Results within your role, contributing Innovative ideas and solutions, and strengthening the broader Team through collaboration and attitude.

This posting reflects an approved, open position within the organization.

About the role

Everand is our subscription app for audiobooks and ebooks. Fable, Everand's sister app, is a social reading community where millions of readers track what they read and talk about books. Together they give us the readers, the catalog, and the community to build the best place to read and listen.

We're hiring a Lead Product Manager to own the Everand app. You'll set its long-term vision, own the experience across every surface, and lead execution from strategy to launch. The goal is an app readers love, where they choose their next book and keep coming back.

We have a loyal base of readers, and millions more people who love books haven't found a product like ours yet. You'll shape how Everand reaches them.

What you'll do

  • Understand Everand's readers deeply: what motivates them, why they stay, and why they leave. Use that understanding in every decision.

  • Set the vision, strategy, and roadmap for the app on iOS and Android, and own the reader experience on every surface, from first open to their next book.

  • Lead a squad of engineers, designers, researchers, and analysts, and own execution: set goals, make trade-offs, and ship well-made work on time.

  • Keep the reader experience human, grounded in readers' taste and the pleasure of reading. Work as an AI-native PM, using AI to speed up research, prototyping, analysis, and building, and bringing it into the product where it helps readers.

  • Decide where to invest by finding the biggest opportunities to make Everand more valuable, for current readers and for readers we don't reach yet.

  • Manage a balanced portfolio of long-term bets and near-term improvements. Test ideas with readers early, and measure success by how their behavior changes.

  • Hold a high bar for app quality, performance, and reliability.

  • Partner with product, engineering, content, and marketing teams to give readers a consistent experience.

  • Bring your squad, partner teams, and leadership along on your strategy, and change it as you learn.

What you bring

  • 7+ years of product management experience on consumer products, including 3+ years owning a consumer native mobile app used by hundreds of thousands of people or more.

  • You are obsessed with consumer apps and study how they work. You can explain what makes the best ones good, and it shows in your product decisions.

  • You understand your audience by what motivates them, and you can point to decisions you changed after time with users.

  • A track record of moving an outcome metric you owned, such as retention, engagement, or conversion.

  • Experience leading product through a major change, such as a platform rebuild, a redesign, or a move into a new audience.

  • Product craft. You work with design from the start, and you've shipped consumer experiences people come back to.

  • You're AI-native. AI is part of how you work every day, and you have a point of view on where it makes a consumer product better for people and where a human touch matters more.

  • Experience with A/B testing and research. You set clear metrics and guardrails, and you know when to rely on qualitative research or judgment instead.

  • Comfort with technical trade-offs, including performance, reliability, and recommendation or personalization systems.

  • Influence without authority across product, engineering, marketing, and leadership.

  • Clear writing and prioritization. You can make the case for a bet and for what you'll leave out.

  • You love books and reading.

Nice to have

  • Experience with subscription businesses: trials, plans, retention, and churn.

  • Experience with audio, video, podcast, or reading apps, including players and offline use.

  • Experience shipping discovery surfaces such as home, browse, search, or personalized feeds.

  • Experience with community or social features in a consumer product.

What success looks like

  • Readers stay longer, engage more, and recommend Everand to others.

  • Readers decide what to read next inside Everand more often.

  • The app is known for its quality.

  • Your squad ships and learns quickly, with a strategy partner teams understand and support.
